Write a "-prm.txt" File for flexMIRT

Source: R/write_flexmirt.R
write.flexmirt.Rd

This function writes a flexMIRT-compatible "-prm.txt" file (Cai, 2017). It supports unidimensional IRT models only. This function was developed by modifying read.flexmirt() from Pritikin & Falk (2020).

Usage

write.flexmirt(
  x,
  file = NULL,
  norm.pop = c(0, 1),
  rePar = TRUE,
  mgroup = FALSE,
  group.name = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame of item metadata (e.g., item parameters, number of categories, model types) for a single group, or a list of such data frames for multiple groups. See est_irt() or simdat() for item metadata format. You can also create metadata using shape_df().

file

A character string giving the path of the file to be written. It must be supplied. flexMIRT parameter files usually end in "-prm.txt".

norm.pop

A numeric vector of length two giving the mean and the variance of the normal ability distribution of a single group, or a list of such vectors, one per group (e.g., norm.pop = list(c(0, 1), c(0, 0.64), c(0.5, 1.44)) for three groups). The second value is written to the variance field of the file. If mgroup = TRUE and a single vector is given, it is used for all groups. Default is c(0, 1).

rePar

Logical. Indicates how the parameters in x are given. If TRUE (default), x is taken to hold flexMIRT slope-intercept values: slopes, intercepts, and logits of the guessing parameters, and for GPCM items the scoring function and intercept values of the nominal model; they are written as they are. If FALSE, x is taken to hold irtQ item metadata (slopes, difficulty or step parameters, and guessing parameters), which is converted to the flexMIRT parameterization. Item metadata from irtQ (for example, from shape_df() or est_irt()) must be written with rePar = FALSE. Note that the meaning is the reverse of the rePar argument of bring.flexmirt(), where TRUE converts the values of the file to irtQ metadata.

mgroup

A logical value indicating whether the file includes multiple groups. Default is FALSE.

group.name

A character vector of group names. If NULL, group names are automatically generated (e.g., "Group1", "Group2", ...).

Value

Called for its side effect of writing the file to file. The value is returned invisibly and is not meant to be used.

Details

The function writes items of the models "1PLM", "2PLM", "3PLM", "DRM", "GRM", and "GPCM". Dichotomous items are written as flexMIRT 3PL ("3PLM" and "DRM") or graded ("1PLM" and "2PLM") items, so bring.flexmirt() reads them back as "3PLM" or "2PLM" items. Every item and every group is written as one line, whatever the width of the console. The parameters are written without rescaling. flexMIRT uses the logistic metric (D = 1); when x was calibrated with another scaling constant, multiply the slopes by that constant before writing.

References

Cai, L. (2017). flexMIRT 3.5 Flexible multilevel multidimensional item analysis and test scoring (Computer software). Chapel Hill, NC: Vector Psychometric Group.

Pritikin, J. N., & Falk, C. F. (2020). OpenMx: A modular research environment for item response theory method development. Applied Psychological Measurement, 44(7-8), 561-562. doi:10.1177/0146621620929431 .

Author

Hwanggyu Lim hglim83@gmail.com

Examples

# \donttest{
## 1. Create a "-prm.txt" file for a single group
##    using the simulated CAT data
# 1-(1) Extract the item metadata
x <- simCAT_MX$item.prm

# 1-(2) Set the name of the "-prm.txt" file
temp_prm <- file.path(tempdir(), "single_group_temp-prm.txt")

# 1-(3) Write the "-prm.txt" file
write.flexmirt(x, file = temp_prm, norm.pop = c(0, 1), rePar = FALSE)

# 1-(4) Read the file back and compare the item parameters
x_back <- bring.flexmirt(file = temp_prm, type = "par")$Group1$full_df
head(x_back)
#>   id cats model     par.1       par.2 par.3 par.4
#> 1 V1    2  2PLM 0.9664715 -0.84085552    NA    NA
#> 2 V2    2  2PLM 0.9152754  1.38435940    NA    NA
#> 3 V3    2  2PLM 1.3454796 -1.25549187    NA    NA
#> 4 V4    2  2PLM 0.7925184  0.07014276    NA    NA
#> 5 V5    2  2PLM 1.0862914  1.71144078    NA    NA
#> 6 V6    2  2PLM 1.1311496 -0.60290796    NA    NA
max(abs(as.matrix(x[, 4:7]) - as.matrix(x_back[, 4:7])), na.rm = TRUE)
#> [1] 1.70888e-07

## 2. Create a "-prm.txt" file for multiple groups
##    using simulated multi-group data
# 2-(1) Extract the item metadata
x <- simMG$item.prm

# Set the name of the "-prm.txt" file
temp_prm <- file.path(tempdir(), "mg_group_temp-prm1.txt")

# Write the "-prm.txt" file, giving the mean and variance of each group
write.flexmirt(x,
  file = temp_prm, norm.pop = list(c(0, 1), c(0.5, 0.64), c(-0.3, 1.69)),
  rePar = FALSE, mgroup = TRUE, group.name = c("GR1", "GR2", "GR3")
)

# Or write the "-prm.txt" file so that
# all groups share the same ability distribution
# and group names are generated automatically
temp_prm <- file.path(tempdir(), "mg_group_temp-prm2.txt")
write.flexmirt(x,
  file = temp_prm, norm.pop = c(0, 1),
  rePar = FALSE, mgroup = TRUE, group.name = NULL
)
# }
